text.tspan: Duty-cycle divider: V_P = 10 V · V_num / V_den
How it works: SW1 feeds −V_den into the integrator for a fraction δ of each cycle. The integrator only stops moving when its average input is zero:
V_num − δ·V_den = 0, so δ = V_num / V_den. SW2 switches 10 V with the same PWM, so after the filter V_P = δ · 10 V = 10 V · V_num / V_den.
The triangle's exact shape and amplitude don't matter (the loop corrects for them); only switch timing and the 10 V reference do.
Parts: TL074 (U1, U2, U4 + the triangle oscillator), LM311 (U3), DG403 (SW1, SW2).
